  *"resolved from the clause structure"*. BSD-2 and BSD-3 are separated by **exactly one piece
  of text** — the non-endorsement clause — and that clause is **also one the instrument
  grades**. Resolve the variant from it and a **BSD-3 truncated at that clause** resolves as a
  BSD-2, is graded against BSD-2's seven clauses, and returns 🔴 `GRANT-PRESENT`: a clean bill
  of health for precisely the truncation the instrument exists to catch. 🟢 **What is sound is
  the asymmetry** — *presence* of the discriminator is proof, since no lesser variant contains
  it; *absence* is ambiguous between a complete BSD-2 and a BSD-3 cut short. So the variant is
  resolved from the payload's own **declaration** (the title line: the only BSD signal
  independent of the graded clauses, and the analogue of GPL's `version 3`), the structural arm
  may answer **only** in the direction that cannot be wrong, and everything else **declines**

  design stays reproducible instead of becoming a remark.

  differ *only* in clauses the instrument grades cannot be variant-resolved from its body at
  all. **Ask what the payload DECLARES that is independent of what you are grading, before
  writing the profile.**

### 🔴 A major publisher's tutor SDK, ungranted — and the method that proved it

**Santillana**, one of the largest education publishers in Spain and Latin America, is the first such
publisher's own AI tutoring code to reach these shelves. **It does not survive procurement:**

| package | npm | declared licence | licence file **in the published tarball** | repository |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@santillana-ai/create-tutor-app` | **v5.9.0, 63 versions** | 🟡 `"license": "MIT"` | 🔴 **NONE** (38,447 B read: README + templates only) | 🔴 `git ls-remote` **prompts for credentials** |

🔴 **Note which package fails.** The MIT claim is on the *scaffolder*; **the package a client's code
would actually import carries no licence at all.** Both are clients for a **proprietary keyed API**,
so a clean grant would have bought an SDK, not a tutoring engine.

🔵 **Two channel facts this established, now `Pattern L` step 11.** **(1)** `git ls-remote`
distinguishes **private from absent** — a credentials prompt means the repository exists and is
**closed**, not dead. **(2)** **The tarball is the artefact and npm serves it even when the repo is
closed**, so the licence that *ships* is readable when the licence the repo *states* is not. Neither
the badge nor the repo could settle Santillana; the artefact did.

### 🔴 The correction, first, because it changes a recommendation

[`agents/top.md`](agents/top.md) told four passes of readers that **"Blackboard has nine servers and
not one verified grant; D2L has six and the only one checked is ungranted"** — and concluded that
both were places where *"a permissively-licensed server would be a genuine contribution."* This pass

| Brightspace / D2L | 6 | **6** | 0 | 0 |

🔴 **Neither was a supply gap. Both were a reading gap.** The census column counted *addresses*; the
sentence reported it as if it counted *grants*. When a count of reads is zero, the honest word is
**unread** — never **ungranted**. That is now `Pattern L` **step 12**.

### 🟢 The gap moved, and the new one is the useful one

**Eleven of the twelve granted servers authenticate as the signed-in student** — the user's own
browser SSO session, no admin API key, read-only because nothing else is reachable from there. They
are personal tools, and a studio cannot hand one to an institution: no tenant identity, no role
boundary, no audit trail, and it breaks when the vendor restyles a login page.

🟢 **Exactly one reads as institution-grade:** [nitsuah/bb-mcp](https://github.com/nitsuah/bb-mcp)
(MIT, 1,063 B) — official Blackboard Learn REST API, OAuth2, role gate, FERPA handling, PII scrub,
JSON audit log, Prometheus metrics, 40 tools including **grade write-back**. 🟡 Maintainer
self-claims, **read and not executed** (`Gap 386-B`). 🔴 And grade write-back is exactly what
[`intel/policy-matrix.tsv`](intel/policy-matrix.tsv) gates by jurisdiction.

🔵 So the restated advice: on these platforms the work is **selection plus hardening**, not building
— written up as 🆕 **Pattern N** in [`compose/patterns.md`](compose/patterns.md), eight concrete
steps from service identity to executing the claims before handover. On D2L step 1 is still a real
build: all six granted servers are student-side.

This base's rule (earned on `open-webui`: BSD-3 + branding clause + CLA at 2,819 B) is that a
non-stock byte length means **read the text**. Correct — and this pass found the benign half:
`AnonymousOnyx22/brightspace-d2l-mcp` at **1,200 B** is MIT **plus an inline derivation notice**, and
`RobertLMcCrary/D2L-MCP` at **2,181 B** is **two complete MIT grants concatenated** (its own plus

condition or a credit?"** — added conditions stop procurement, added credits are obligations you
inherit silently and no identifier-based SBOM will show you. `Pattern L` **step 11**.
🔵 The same read is a cheap **fork-family fingerprint**: three Brightspace slugs return a
byte-identical payload still holding `© 2026 Rohan Muppa`, so a slug census over-counts the supply.

### 🔴 `ACTION p377-D`: the prediction, and the instrument defect that flipped it

🟢 **Registered the way this base requires** — three limbs, each with its own refutation
condition, committed in `729d9fa` with no leg output in the tree. It also recorded, **before any
result**, a defect in the action it was discharging: `p377-D`'s single condition conflated the
**pooled rate** with the **dispersion**, and those are independent.

| | `p377` (zh · ko · pt · es) | `p378` (hi · ar · id · fr) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Addresses probed | 9 | 17 |
| NEW | 6 · **67 %** | 6 · **35 %** |
| Answer set in the leg's own language | productive in every cell | **2 of 17 · 12 %** |
| Rows clearing the agent bar | 1 | **0** |

🔴 **LIMB 1 REFUTED.** This pass predicted a pooled NEW rate **above 77 %**, on the mechanism
that Hindi, Arabic and Indonesian neighbourhoods had never been swept. The rate is **35.3 %**.
🔵 **The mechanism was sound and its premise was wrong:** those neighbourhoods were not
unswept, they are **not reached**. Three of four legs landed back in the English neighbourhood
this base has swept hardest.

🔴 **LIMB 2 FLIPPED.** It read **CONFIRMED** at a 16.7-point spread until this pass found that
`make carried` had graded a carried address `NEW`. Corrected, the four rates are
**40.0 / 33.3 / 33.3 / 33.3** — a **6.7-point** band against a registered threshold of 15.
🟢 **The draft had already declared limb 2 not load-bearing**, on the registered ground that
*"the `ar` and `id` legs have denominators of 3: ONE address moving either way changes the
verdict"*. One address moved. 🔵 So `p377-D`'s single condition falls **both ways at once**:
"uniform axis" is **confirmed on dispersion** and **refuted on level**.

🟢 **LIMB 3 CONFIRMED, at zero of six.** Two addresses ship no grant anywhere in the tree —
`p275` full-tree enumeration, 38 and 28 files, `NONE_IN_TREE`. One is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Two are
curated lists. One is a 2022 non-AI e-learning site.

🔴 **The finding a successor must not soften.** An in-language query is a different instrument
**only where the language has an indexed developer-forge population**. 🟢 It holds for `zh`,
`ko`, `pt` and partly `id`/`fr`. 🔴 It does **not** hold for `hi` or `ar`. A successor reading
`p377` alone would run a Hindi leg for an India engagement and buy the English index at full
price. 🟢 And the dial to choose a leg by is the **in-language fraction**, never the NEW rate:
the `ar` leg (zero foreign reach) and the `id` leg (a genuinely Indonesian repository) scored
the **same** NEW rate.

### 🔴 The finding, in one sentence

🔴 **`p374` reasoned that its one German fact arrived through a French outlet because a
cross-border press channel covered Germany *in the language of the query*; `p375` ran the French
leg that account predicts should win, and it returned the identical fact from the identical
single page (`actuia.com`) that the English leg had already found.**

🟢 **So the unit of analysis was wrong for three passes, and it is not a language.** A leg is
productive when **at least one indexed outlet** covers that jurisdiction's education policy in a
language the query can reach. Query language matters only insofar as it changes *which* outlets
are reachable — and for Germany the reachable set has **size one in both languages tested**.

| Draw | Pass | Language | Verdict | German facts | Retrieving outlet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `p373` | English | 🔴 **NIL** | 0 (returned North American state policy) | — |
| 2 | `p374` | English | 🟡 PARTIAL | 1 | `actuia.com` (French) |
| 3 | `p375` | English | 🟡 PARTIAL | 1 | `actuia.com` (French) |
| F1 | `p375` | **French** | 🟡 PARTIAL | 1, **no richer** | `actuia.com` — **the same page** |

🔴 **The sharp consequence, which a successor should not soften: a jurisdiction served by one
outlet is one outlet away from a nil.** That is what draw 1 was. It is a **fragility** property
of Germany's coverage, not evidence about German as a language — and `Gap 476`, `ACTION PJ`,
`p373` and `p374` were each reading a different shadow of it.

### 🟢 The commercial reading, and it is a build constraint rather than a market figure

🟢 **Four jurisdictions, three legal systems, no shared drafting body, and the same boundary: an
AGE FLOOR on autonomous pupil use of generative AI.** China's MOE guide bars primary pupils from
independently using open-ended generation; Brazil's `Parecer CNE/CP nº 15/2026` prohibits
autonomous use to the end of 5th grade; France's framework permits it **from classe de
quatrième**; New York's `A.9190` would bar most classroom AI below grade 9. 🔵 **Three of the
four land in the same band — end of primary, roughly ages 11–13.**

🟢 **This is `p374`'s convergence repeated on a second, independent axis.** `p374` found that
three legal systems agree an AI system **may inform a mark and may not decide one**. `p375` finds
they also agree on **who may drive the tool at all**. 🟢 **Neither is satisfiable with a policy
document**, and `Pattern 15` builds the second one the same way `Pattern 14` built the first: as
a **permission an auditor can check in minutes** — a per-stage virtual key at the gateway with no
generative model attached for the youngest cohort, rather than a prompt instruction or a hidden
button.

🟢 **And France hands an open-source studio the most directly commercial sentence in this base's
EMEA section:** its national framework **recommends free and open-source tools**, favours frugal
use, and tolerates consumer services only where **no personal or sensitive data** is entered.
🔵 It converges with Futuresource's **small-language-model** finding (institutions seeking
*"secure, curriculum-specific AI environments"*, driven by governance needs) and with
**Latam-GPT**'s sovereignty premise. 🟢 **Small, self-hosted and auditable is the one direction
where a permissively-licensed stack is the *compliant* answer and not merely the cheaper one.**

🔴 **Graded honestly: every jurisdictional cell above is SECONDARY.** No primary instrument text
was retrieved for any of the four floors — government egress is `Gap 241`, the Chinese and German
documents are `Gap 497` and `Gap 496`. 🔴 **France rests on a single source, and that source is a
bill's explanatory memorandum describing the ministry's framework rather than the framework.**
🔴 **And one circulating claim is refused rather than reported:** a commercial site asserts a
nationwide mandatory weekly AI class in China for grades 3–12 from autumn 2026, with **no MOE
document behind it** in the result set.

### 🟢 What a reader should take from it

🟢 **The question was wrong for 168 passes.** Japan's English and Japanese legs were **both
productive** and returned **different fact classes** — English gave policy milestones, Japanese
gave the only operational figure either produced (**generative-AI pilot schools 66 → 281**).
🟢 **So an in-language leg is not a fallback for a failed English leg. It is a different
instrument, and both should run.** That is now enforced: `J3` refuses any claim that a language
is *redundant* unless both legs ran **and returned the same fact class**.

### 🔴 The commercial reading, and the part of it that is a correction

🔴 **EMEA: the obligation `p373` sold yesterday was rewritten three months before it wrote it.**
`p373` pitched *"Art. 4's AI-literacy duty binds providers AND deployers, and a school is a
deployer — it is live now"*. **Regulation (EU) 2026/1744** (OJ **2026-07-24**, in force
**2026-07-27**) replaced Article 4: *"ensure a sufficient level"* became *"take measures to
**support the development** of AI literacy of their **staff**"*, and the Commission FAQ of
**2026-07-27** says it *"does not require a specific level for any given person"*.
🟢 **The engagement survives in a better shape:** it is **evidence-production** — a register of
who operates which system, a documented programme, training records an auditor can read —
live now, supervised from **August 2026**, with Annex III still at **2027-12-02**.
🔴 **Graded: all secondary.** The operative wording was not retrieved (`Gap 241`), and sources
conflict on the in-force day. 🟢 **`p373`'s sentence is marked corrected, not deleted.**

🟢 **The convergence that is worth more than any market figure.** Three legal systems that share
no sources have independently drawn the **same** operational boundary — **an AI system may
inform an assessment and may not decide one**: Brazil's *excessive* tier bars fully automated
promotion-or-retention decisions and reserves marks to teachers; the US district statutes'
recurring shape is human oversight plus no automated high-stakes decision; EU **Annex III** puts
education use cases in the high-risk register. 🟢 **One architecture sells in all three**, and
`Pattern 14` is it.
🔴 **And it cannot be delivered by policy or configuration.** A GitLab advisory on
`lti-consumer-xblock` reports that **any** LTI tool on an Open edX platform can post a grade back
for **any** XBlock given the `resource_link_id`. 🟢 So the AI component must hold **no
grade-write scope at all** — a permission an auditor can check in minutes, not a promise.

### 🔴 The finding, in one sentence

🔴 **`Gap 483`'s "46 dead addresses" contained ten strings that were never addresses — and
this base was already rejecting five of them in a GREEN STANDING GATE.**
`p351-address-shape`, run by `gate-address-shape` on every `make hooks`, classifies

`repos/HKUDS`) and `your-username/SafeTutors` as **`PLACEHOLDER-OWNER`**. The other five are
slugs this base **fabricated** as negative controls for its own existence oracles.
🔴 **Plus two LIVE repositories that hold zero commits and therefore answer `rc=0` with an
empty ref advertisement**, which `p230` called `GONE` and `p371` called `NO-REMOTE`.
🟢 **34 are genuinely absent, and `git clone` names the live class itself:** *"warning: You
appear to have cloned an empty repository."*

### 🟢 What a reader should take from it

🟢 **An absence verdict is three questions, and running them together is what produced a
wrong figure twice.** *Is the string an address? Does the address answer? Is a dead address
being cited as a live claim, or as a record of a measurement?* 🔵 The third question is the
one that decides the remedy, and `gate-dead-citation`'s `I2` answers it mechanically: **zero**
of the 34 absent addresses is a linked row on any live shelf. They sit in append-only
histories, where rewriting them would destroy the very trend those files exist to record.
🟢 **`Gap 483`'s prescribed remedy — "repoint or retract" — was therefore mostly already
satisfied by this base's structure; the one repair the shelves needed was an ADDITION.**

🔴 **The defect worth copying out of this pass is `E2`, and `p372` can state it more sharply
than `p371` could.** 🔵 The failure mode is NOT that knowledge goes unrecorded — the
`repos/*` rejections sit in a **green standing gate** and the Opencast successor sits in
**committed prose**. 🔴 **It is that two instruments measuring the same corpus never read
each other's verdicts:** `p351`'s address-shape census and every absence census here have
run side by side for scores of passes without one ever consulting the other, so a string
this base formally rejects as a non-address was still counted as a dead address. 🟢 `p372`
joins them in `I1`, which cross-checks every filed class against what the classifier would
assign.

🔴 **And the narrower version of the same thing, which `p371` named while committing it:** `apereo/opencast → opencast/opencast` was **proven on 2026-10-15** by
`p230` and written into prose at `intel/open-gaps.md:4347`. It was never written into any
register a gate reads, so six days later `p371` counted it among 46 unknowns and opened a gap
to adjudicate it again. 🔵 *"Committed knowledge that is not wired into the next instrument
gets paid for twice"* — this is the third consecutive pass to pay it (`p369`'s `LICENSE.TXT`,
`p371`'s `https://` host rule, now this). 🟢 **`p372` answers with a register and an invariant
rather than a fourth restatement**, and proves the successor from the successor's own
committed `NOTICES` — because `p370`'s ref-set fingerprint, this base's usual identity proof,
**cannot** settle a rename whose old address has no ref set.

🟢 **And the control that had never been run is the reason any of this is safe.** Every
absence verdict here rested on an untested assumption: that a renamed or transferred
repository still answers at its old address. Measured at `p372`, it does —
`Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT` returns 12 137 refs and `hwchase17/langchain` returns 27 996
at their old addresses — so `NO-REMOTE` **excludes** rename and transfer. 🔵 **The verdicts
are safe because that was measured, not because it was assumed.**

🟢 **The other half of the pass is that a thirteen-pass nil turned out to be about the
query.** `Gap 476` hypothesised that the regional legs' near-nils came from a monolingual
query assumption. Run side by side in one pass: the prescribed **English** EMEA leg returned
**0** education-specific dated facts; the **German** leg returned **4**, including the German
school sector's own published position on when educational AI counts as high-risk — the
substance `Gap 241` has been unable to reach for six passes, from a host outside the blocked
EU institutional set. The **Portuguese** LATAM leg returned **Brazil's CNE school-AI
regulation**: risk classification for school technology, no unsupervised AI below the 5th
year, and **no autonomous AI grading of work that requires interpretation** — which means the
automated-grading recipes on this base cannot be sold into Brazilian schools as autonomous
graders at all. 🔴 **This base has found the language axis three times and made it standing
zero times** (`P521`, `ACTION ZZ-cc`, `Gap 476`). 🟢 `I4` now refuses a published regional nil
unless an in-language leg was run, and it was negative-controlled: removing the German row
turns the gate red.

🔴 **The commercial reading, and it is the part a studio should act on.** `p371` found
credentialing to be the layer these shelves were missing. 🔴 **`p372` finds that the layer's
runnable starting points are the part that has disappeared:** Caliper Analytics is absent in

interoperability layer in education, budget to implement the standard from its specification,
not to adopt a reference implementation** — and treat *"there is a reference implementation"*

### 🔴 The finding, in one sentence

🟢 `p349`'s own docstring names the mechanism its gate catches: *"GitHub keeps every
former address of a transferred or renamed repository answering FOREVER, by redirect."*
🔴 **A redirect serves one repository, so the old address must answer with the same ref
set — and five register rows answer with their own.** `dymayo/moodler-mcp` carries **2**
refs against the canonical side's **62** at the same `HEAD`; `sharziki/purdue-mcp`'s
`refs/pull/1/head` **is** `rohanmuppa/purdue-mcp`'s branch tip, so one of that pair opened
a pull request against the other. 🔵 **Two repositories in a contributor relationship
cannot be one address and its redirect.**

### 🔴 The second finding, which is about this base rather than GitHub

🔴 **`p367` discharged this gate by editing the shelf in the wrong direction.** It wrote
that `agents/top.md` *"carried `INGInious/INGInious` as a live row address"* and fixed the
row to cite `UCL-INGI/INGInious`. 🟢 **Measured this pass: fetching
`github.com/UCL-INGI/INGInious` lands on `INGInious/INGInious`** (243 ★, breadcrumb

gate went green anyway, because `ALIAS_REGISTER` pointed at `p349`'s register, which has
no `INGInious` row at all** — while `p350` had built a register three times larger and
nothing was ever pointed at it. Both rows are restored and the default now points at
`p370`'s register.

was.** `p363` found the first of the opposite kind.
[`eth-nlped/mathdial`](https://github.com/eth-nlped/mathdial) (**95 ★**, EMNLP Findings

**share-alike ships inside a client deliverable**. 🟢 Hence the new `grant_channel`
column in the evidence file — the channel is as much a datum as the licence name.

### 🔴 A probe this pass had to throw away

🔴 **`p363`'s first licence sweep reported *"all 11 paths 404"* across eight addresses and
was not entitled to.** The loop tested `[ "$c" = "200" ]` and read every non-200 as

### 🔴 Three new trends, and §16 is the first to RETIRE a capability this base shelves

- **§16 — the AI-detector market is being abandoned by its own customers.** Yale, Cornell
  and UW–Madison now discourage or bar detection scores in misconduct cases; a Stanford
  study found detectors flagged **61 % of essays by non-native English speakers** as
  machine-written. 🟢 **The distinction is the finding:** *authorship attribution* is
  collapsing because it cannot be made at an acceptable false-positive rate across
  language backgrounds — **an equity failure, not a model-quality one, so a better model
  does not fix it.** *Supervision* (proctoring) and *similarity* (plagiarism) are
  untouched, because neither claims to know what produced the text. Of this base's four
  detection-adjacent rows, **three survive and one carries demand-side risk.** New
  **Pattern 12** is the replacement build.
- **§17 — AI marking has acquired a disclosure duty and a measured anchoring bias.** The
  University of Newcastle (Australia) requires disclosure of AI use in marking **with a
  student opt-out**; a **1 339-teacher** experiment found a harsh AI grade **survives
  review more often when labelled as AI**. 🔴 That inverts the assumption every
  grading-agent design rests on — that disclosure plus human review makes automation safe.
- **§18 — non-OSI licensing has a second shape.** `PolyForm Noncommercial` on the most
  capable platform in the capture leg, and an **AGPL-3.0 open-core *connector***. 🔵 The
  second inverts this base's governing rule: a protocol boundary holds a copyleft
  **platform** at arm's length, but when the copyleft thing **is the MCP server** it sits
  *inside* the deliverable, on the wrong side of that boundary. **Check the connector's
  licence before the platform's** — smaller component, larger risk.

uniformity is the tell — a real distribution shift does not move five buckets by one

### 🔴 What this pass found that no item asked for

🔴 **`classroomio/classroomio` declares a different licence on every channel it has**, all read
first-hand today: root `LICENSE` = **`AGPL-3.0`** (`34 523` B · `8486a10c4393`), root `package.json`
= **`MIT`**, `apps/api/package.json` = **`ISC`**. 🔵 **A dependency scanner reads manifests — that is
what a scanner is for — so the automated answer here is *permissive*, twice over, and the one channel
carrying the network-copyleft term is the one a scanner does not treat as authoritative.** 🔴 A studio
that screens this repository the normal way concludes `MIT`, brands the LMS, hosts it, and acquires an
undisclosed §13 obligation. 🟢 **`p279` had the manifest half and drew the wrong conclusion from it**
(*"both permissive, so nothing you may do changes"*) **because it never read the `LICENSE`; that row
now carries the correction.** 🔵 **And it surfaced only because `gate-shelf-consistency` went red on
this pass's own new cell** — the gate working exactly as designed, on the pass that wrote it.

🔴 **`MIT` title spelling is diverging**: four shapes read today — bare, parenthesised (`OpenHands`),
**indented four spaces** (`microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners`), and absent entirely (`crewAI`).

🔴 **Rung lessons, three in one hour:** `frappe/lms` serves its grant at **`license.txt`** — lowercase
stem *and* extension, which a ROOT `LICENSE` ladder misses; `learnhouse/learnhouse` serves its grant
on **`dev`**, not `main`; and `UD_Portuguese-CINTIL`'s rung resolves to a `224` B **bare citation**.
🔵 **A rung that resolves is not a grant that exists** — the cheapest reusable lesson of the pass.

🟢 **`p311`'s rule holds at `n=5` and gained its converse.** `AGPL-3.0` now reads at five byte lengths
for one grant (`33 893` is the new low, `frappe/lms`); `8486a10c4393` is now served by a **fifth**
unrelated repository. 🔴 **And two `MPL-2.0` payloads sit at IDENTICAL byte length and are different
files** — so byte length does not reliably answer *"is this the same file?"* either.

🔴 **The structural finding for an engagement:** the obligation in an education AI project does not
come from the AI. The agent, tutoring, authoring and infrastructure tiers are **`9/9` permissive**;
the learner-facing **LMS tier is `AGPL-3.0` in every row this pass read**. 🟢 **§13 attaches to what
the client already runs, not to what the studio is adding** — which makes it an early question about
the existing estate rather than a risk the AI work introduces.

## Pass 311 — 2026-10-19 — **THE TWO BIGGEST FAMILIES CAME BACK CLEAN AND BOTH REAL DEFECTS WERE IN SMALL FAMILIES THE PASS REACHED BY ACCIDENT; ONE INVISIBLE BYTE SWITCHED THE TITLE CHANNEL OFF AND DROPPED TWO INSTRUMENTS ONTO THE LADDER IT EXISTS TO REPLACE**

**One-line summary:** 🟢 **`MIT` (5 549 cells) and `Apache-2.0` (2 335) ran through the dynamic arm
for the first time — `7 884` cells, 61 % of every licence cell this base publishes — and the result
is ZERO defects across 8 payload readers.** 🔴 **The hour was worth spending and the REASON it was
ranked first was wrong:** `family_coverage.py` prints its queue in descending cell order, which
ranks **blast radius**, and `ACTION p310-R` read it as a risk ranking. 🔴 **The pass's one real
defect was in `MPL-2.0`, `161` cells — `p153/classify_body` read every `MPL-2.0` payload as
`GPL-3.0`, because `MPL-2.0` §1.12 names the GNU licences in its *«Secondary License»* definition
and the loop took the first marker anywhere in 4 000 characters: Mozilla title at char `0`, GNU
phrase at char `2 341`, list order beating document position.** Third instance of that class in
three instruments. 🔴 **The SECOND defect is a shape new to this base and worse: a UTF-8 BOM on
`openSIS-Classic`'s `GPL-2.0` payload made `p150.title_licence()` return `None` — `str.strip()`
does not remove `U+FEFF` — so `p191`, which IMPORTS that title read, fell through to its own body

wrong; it was silently switched OFF, and the fallback was the ladder it replaces.** 🔵 **And that
row arrived as a refutation of this pass's own writing:** the pass wrote *"no payload at any probed
rung"* and **`gate-enumeration` walked the tree and named two grants under `docs/`**. 🔴 **`p310`'s
own suite also asserted `"MIT" not in corpus`, so discharging the item `p310` ranked first turned a
green gate red** — second instance in two passes of the exact pattern `ACTION p310-R` item 4 was
registered to hunt. 🟢 **New gate `gate-permissive-arm`; 32 controls; 20/20 gates green at
publication.**

## Pass 310 — 2026-10-19 — **`p309` REPAIRED THE RUNG AND NOT THE MECHANISM: FIVE LINES BELOW ITS FIX, THE SAME LADDER GRADED A NONCOMMERCIAL GRANT AS PUBLIC DOMAIN — AND THEN THIS PASS HAD TO REFUTE ITS OWN SUPPLY HEADLINE AGAINST ITS OWN SHELVES**

**One-line summary:** 🔴 **`p306-licence-probe` graded [`aclascollege/aegis-graph`](https://github.com/aclascollege/aegis-graph)
— `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, `19 347` B `41003d4a7474`, *"Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International"* on
its first line — as `CC0-1.0`, a public-domain dedication.** The rung was
`elif "cc0" in low or "public domain dedication" in low:` over the whole body, ordered before the
CC-BY rungs, and **every CC 4.0 legalcode names `CC0` exactly once in its own boilerplate**, so
no CC 4.0 payload could ever reach its own rung. 🔴 **`p124-correction-form-marker` refuted that
exact test on `2026-10-11`, was BUILT on it (its first cut returned CC0 for 9 of 13 rows), ships
`cc_version.resolve()`, and registered it as instance 3 of `ACTION AG` labelled `DOCUMENT-TEXT`
— 186 passes ago.** 🔵 **`p309` concluded *"a classifier is canonical data too; import the
discriminator, never restate it"*, applied it to the GNU rungs, and did not read the next five
lines.** 🔴 **And the direction matters: `p309`'s defect EXCLUDED usable supply; this one ADMITS
unusable supply into a client deliverable.** 🟢 **Realised loss re-measured on all seven
published CC0 rows: ZERO — and that audit found a second defect, below.** 🟢 **New standing gate
`gate-family-coverage`; 58 controls; 19/19 gates green at publication.**

include the traps the original was built for.** `Submitty` and `kolibri` were not arbitrary choices —

### 🔵 Why `ACTION p291` is a correction and not `p290` again

`p290` asked **what the grant covers** when the content is gitlinks, and answered it with a
two-condition rule. 🟢 The first condition — read the submodule's own payload — was right.
🔴 The second — that its `HEAD` must equal the pin — encodes a limitation of the *tool* `p290`
happened to use (`git ls-remote` returns `HEAD`) as a property of the *evidence*. A pinned SHA
is a perfectly good ref on `raw.githubusercontent.com`. So the grant that a
`git clone --recurse-submodules` actually lands on can be read directly, and equality of `HEAD`
and pin on the day of measurement is **timing, not evidence**. That is control `C7`, and it
rejects `p290`'s own two rows if they are ever re-asserted without being re-read.

### 🔴 What this pass's own gates did to this pass

🟢 **`p283`'s ladder ratchet rejected `ACTION p291` once, and it was right.** The new
instrument graded `STANDING:SINGLE-SPELLING`, taking the ceiling from 17 to 18, over a **single
capitalised licence filename inside a human-readable finding message**. The module has **no
path ladder at all** — it never probes for a grant, it reads `payload_path` out of the evidence
TSV. 🔵 This is `p289`'s situation exactly (its prose regex looked like a ladder until it was
written as `licen[cs]e`) and the remedy is the same: say it in words that are not a filename.
Reworded to *"root grant"*; the ceiling is back to 17 and the reason is recorded **in the
source**, so a later pass does not "restore" the capitalised word.

🔴 **And `p291`'s own shelf check was wrong on its first run: 7 findings, 6 of them false.**
It was written **line**-scoped, and `compose/patterns.md` names the gitlinks **two lines below**
the citation it flagged. A line is not the unit a reader reads. Rescoped to the blank-line
**block**, it drops all 6 and keeps the one real finding. 🔵 A second defect of the same kind
was caught beside it: the check recognised only its own jargon, so a cell saying *"It is a
pointer; the seven sector configurations are separate repositories"* — which names the boundary
**better** than the word "gitlink" does — was flagged. A gate that only matches its own
vocabulary measures the vocabulary.

🔵 **One scope decision, stated because it is a judgement call.** On the append-only shelves
(`agents/trending.md`, `repos/trending.md`) the shelf arm reads only the newest `## Pass`
section — **`p279-absence-claims`'s convention, adopted verbatim rather than invented twice**.
Those files keep history by design; a gate failing on passes 243 onward would be red on arrival
and disabled within a pass. The historical `org:iblai` cell is therefore **reported and left
standing**: history is the record of what each pass believed, and the gate's job is that the
*next* citation cannot repeat it.

### 🔵 Why `ACTION p290` is a new axis and not `p289` again

Every licence instrument on these shelves asks **where the grant is** (`p215` path, `p969`
root-only, `p742` body-vs-reference, `p259` location class) or **what the grant says** (`p287`
family, `p289` authority-vs-restatement). 🔴 **A gitlink asks neither** — it asks **what the
grant covers**, with the payload present, root-level, authoritative and verbatim.

🟢 **And unlike `p289`'s catalogue badge, this question is answerable in bulk**, because a
submodule pin is an exact SHA. The rule: a submodule's grant is verified when its own payload
is read first-hand **and** the HEAD it was read at equals the pinned gitlink. Where the
submodule has moved past its pin, the pin is an **unread commit** → `UNVERIFIED-AT-PIN`.

### 🔴 What this pass could NOT do

🔴 **This base's own `ladder.sh` and `enumerate.sh` would not execute in this environment** —
the runner refused to run shell scripts from the clone, so `make gate-online`, `make enumerate`
and `make provenance-sweep` were unavailable. The measurement was re-implemented directly: a
**13-rung** licence ladder × 2 refs over `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and
`git clone --depth 1` + `git ls-tree -r` for tree enumeration.
🔴 **13 rungs is not `make reach`'s 55**, so **no absence in this pass carries 55-rung
authority**; positives are payloads read first-hand, negatives are labelled 13-rung negatives
in the evidence. 🟢 `make hooks` itself ran clean — **all 12 gates PASS**, before and after the
shelf writes.

🔴 **`github.com/trending`, `github.com` HTML and `api.github.com/repos` all answer `403`.** No
star count in this pass is first-hand and **none is published.** 🟢 Two channels do answer and
they agreed on every existence verdict: `raw.githubusercontent.com` and `git ls-remote`.

### 🔵 What a studio takes from this pass

**The compliance posture stopped being the deliverable and became a dependency.** Three MIT
sibling agents — `application-reader`, `special-education`, `retention` — each **refuse the
sole-basis act in their own prompt**, which is the one engineering requirement the EU AI Act,
Vietnam's sole-basis clause and the Oklahoma/Maryland rules all converge on. 🔴 **What none of
them has is the record**: *"log every intervention — date, method, response, outcome"* is an
instruction to a model, not a schema, an append-only store or an artefact an auditor can be

written out as [`P45`](compose/patterns.md), [`P46`](compose/patterns.md) and
[`P47`](compose/patterns.md).** 🟡 And quote the **submodule**, never the superproject.

## Pass 287 — 2026-10-18 — **ITEM 1 DISCHARGED BOTH WAYS, AND THE SAME FUNCTION WAS ALSO REFUSING A REAL MIT GRANT — THE DIRECTION THIS BASE HAS NEVER COUNTED**

**One-line summary:** `p286` ranked *"multilingual restriction vocabulary + an `UNREADABLE-BODY`

candidates with the fixed instrument, found that **the same function had been grading a verbatim
MIT grant as `UNCLASSIFIED` for thirty passes.** `make hooks` is **green** (54 PASS, exit 0), run
before any edit and again after every one.

### 🟢 Item 1 discharged — and the shell gate was INVENTING PERMISSION over a total prohibition

🔴 **Reproduced first, exactly as `p286` left it.** `sira313/rapkumer`'s 3 140-byte Indonesian
payload, whose §3 is titled `LARANGAN PENGGUNAAN KOMERSIAL` — *prohibition of commercial use* —
scanned as `UNCLASSIFIED:no-family-no-restriction` with **zero hits**, while an English control
fired `RESTRICTED:added-restriction` correctly. **The logic was sound; the vocabulary's language
was the whole defect.**

🟢 **Both halves, as the backlog required, with their downstream consumers:**

| | |
|---|---|
| 🟢 **Vocabulary keyed BY LANGUAGE** | `RESTRICTION_TERMS_BY_LANGUAGE`, **10 arms**. The English arm is `p257`'s, **moved not rewritten**, so no English verdict in this base's history changes. zh/ja/ko/es/pt/fr/de/it ported **phrase for phrase** from `lib/license_family.sh::commercial_use_ok` (`P240`/`P241`) |
| 🟢 **The `id` arm neither implementation had** | Added to the Python instrument **and to the shell lib in the same change** |
| 🟢 **`UNREADABLE-BODY:no-vocabulary-for-this-language`** | A verdict, not a silence. Adding arms **shrinks** the uncovered set and can never **empty** it |
| 🟢 **The port measured BOTH WAYS** (`p637`) | The suite asserts every shell phrase is reachable from the Python vocabulary, that the shell lib really carries them, and that both gained `id` |

🔴 **And the measurement that says why this mattered.** On the live payload, the **shell** gate —
the one inside `make hooks` — went **`0 = ALLOWED` → `1 = RESTRICTED`**. 🔵 It had been **inventing
permission over a text that prohibits commercial use in any form**, which is `P241`'s own warning
reproduced in a language `P241` did not reach. Negative control
(*"Penggunaan komersial diizinkan tanpa batasan apa pun"*) stays `ALLOWED` in both.

🟢 **Second real payload for the `zh` arm:** `heronerar/OpenGaokao`'s 15 992-byte, 92.9 %-CJK
`OpenGaokao-SAL-1.0` — `禁止商业使用`, and its body states it is **not an OSI-approved licence**.
Also previously `UNCLASSIFIED`, zero hits.

🔵 **Why a cheap language test is sound here**, stated because a later pass will want to replace
it: `scan` asks it **one** question — covered or not — so the overwhelmingly likely error
(confusing `es`/`pt`/`it`, which share function words) **cannot change a verdict**. Of the two
that can, the costly one is guarded by demanding **positive evidence** of a covered language and
defaulting to uncovered. **`P241`'s rule, moved onto the language axis.**

## Pass 284 — 2026-10-18 — **THE EIGHT-PASS RED STREAK WAS PINNING THE WRONG POPULATION, `p283`'S `NOTICE` HEADLINE WAS HALF AN INSTRUMENT ERROR, AND THE ONE LEG `p283` TOLD THIS PASS TO REPLACE BROKE A FOUR-PASS NIL**

**One-line summary:** all three of `p283`'s top items are discharged, and each one turned out to be
**wrong about itself in the same direction** — the remedy it asked for was smaller than the defect it
revealed. The census streak was a gate firing on zero risk; the `NOTICE` family was one real defect
plus one false verdict against the instrument that invented the rule; and the regional battery's
four-pass *"Africa is empty"* was a property of the query. `make hooks` was run **before any edit**
(green on `p283`'s state) and after every edit.

### 🟢 Item 1 discharged — and the eight-pass streak has a cause, not just a remedy

🔴 `p283` registered: *"DERIVE these three literals from the Makefile instead of typing them."*
🟢 Done. 🔴 **But writing it exposed why eight passes failed, and it is not forgetfulness.**

| | |
|---|---|
| the three literals | `221` test files · `40` gated · `181` ungated |
| what they pinned | **a count of FILES ON DISK** |
| what the eight added suites did to EXPOSURE | 🟢 **nothing** — p261, p262, p275, p277, p278, p279, p280 and p283 each wrote *"`ungated` stays at 181"* |
| what already caught the only at-risk shape | `--verify`'s **`UNPINNED`**, by name, with no literal involved |

🔵 **Eight consecutive passes were stopped by a red gate over a change that moved the risk by zero.**
A gate that fires on every change and on no risk trains its reader to bump the number — which is
exactly what eight passes did. 🟢 The replacement is a **cross-check between two readings of the
gate's reach, written in opposite directions**: `is_gated` walks disk files and searches the recipes;
the new `derive_gated` walks recipe lines and emits files that exist. **They agree, suite by suite,
40 = 40, with no literal anywhere** — and a **positive control injects `p280`'s exact false credit
(`p791-registry-id-provenance/test_provenance.py`) and requires the agreement to break**, so the
defect the pins uniquely caught is still caught. Suite **43 → 46**. The `71`-suite exposure
population **stays pinned**: a change there *is* a change in risk.
Evidence: [`census-derivation.2026-10-18-p284.tsv`](evidence/census-derivation.2026-10-18-p284.tsv).

### 🟢 Items 2 and 3 discharged — one real defect, one false verdict, and a ratchet instead of a pin

🔴 `p283` published *"**Not one `NOTICE` ladder on this base can find `NOTICE.TXT`**"*, `notice` being
*"the only family at **0.0 %**"*. 🟢 **Half was real. Half was the measuring instrument.**

| ladder | `p283` | 🟢 `p284` |
|---|---|---|
| `p229-grant-ladder-reach/ladder.sh` `TIER_A` | `CASE-UNVARIED` | 🟢 **`CASE-CLOSED`** — a **REAL** defect: it carried `NOTICE NOTICE.txt` only. `NOTICE.TXT` + `notice.txt` added (+2 requests/slug); `pass256-ladder-closure` green at **38/38** |
| `p1057-licence-path-case/path_case.py` | `STEM-ONLY` | 🟢 **`GENERATED-CASE-VARIED`** — 🔴 a **FALSE POSITIVE against the instrument that invented case-closure**: `candidate_paths` is a cross product over `STEMS × EXTS × _casings(stem) × {ext, ext.upper()}` and **already generates `NOTICE.TXT`** |

🔵 **Why the audit misread it — and the caveat was its own.** `p283`'s audit reads the **literal**
path vocabulary, and its docstring says so: *"An instrument that builds its paths by concatenation is
reported as what its literals show."* A cross product has no literal to read. 🔴 **The caveat sat in
the prose and was ignored at the point of publication**, which is this base's recurring shape — so it
is now **enforced in code** as a `GENERATED-CASE-VARIED` verdict whose predicate requires **both** an
extension-case and a stem-case idiom. **13 new controls in `p1057`'s own suite (16 → 29)** assert the
**generated** ladder directly. `notice` is now **1 `CASE-CLOSED`, 0 `STEM-ONLY`, 0 `CASE-UNVARIED`**.

🟢 **Item 2 as a RATCHET, not a pin** — [`ratchet.tsv`](compose/code/p283-ladder-case-audit/ratchet.tsv),
six bounds, checked in `make gate-ladder-case`. 🔵 **That choice is item 1's lesson carried across:**
an exact count goes red on every added instrument (the `p252` streak); a **floor** on good verdicts
and a **ceiling** on defective ones goes red **only on a real regression**. Base-wide `CASE-CLOSED`
**20 → 21**, `STEM-ONLY` **24 → 22**.
Evidence: [`ladder-census.2026-10-18-p284.tsv`](evidence/ladder-census.2026-10-18-p284.tsv).

### 🟢 Item 8 was the highest-value item on the list: the gap-directed leg broke Africa open

🔴 `p283` ranked *"replace one regional leg with a gap-directed leg (Africa)"* **eighth**, and it
returned more than the four mandated legs combined. On its first run: the **AU Continental Education
Strategy `2026–2035`**, the **AU Continental AI Strategy**, **Kenya's National AI Strategy
`2025–2030`**, **South Africa's DBE coding & robotics (Grades R–9)**, **North-West University's
first SA university AI policy (Jan 2026)**, a **pan-African ethical AI curriculum** (`arXiv
2604.27708`) and an **open-source-LLM recommendation for African universities** (`arXiv 2510.18902`).

🔵 **The methodological finding is the bigger one.** Four passes published Africa as empty on the
strength of a leg that **had never asked about Africa** — it asked about EMEA. That is `p254`'s *the
base inherits its own conclusions about what is impossible*. 🟢 **New rule, recorded in
[`intel/trends.md`](intel/trends.md) as `T-p284b`: before a gap is published as a property of the
world, one leg must have addressed it by name.** 🟡 And the gap **changed shape rather than closed** —
everything returned is policy, curriculum or preprint; there is still **no production open-source
education agent built for an African deployment**.

### 🟢 LATAM: the ranked homologation watch moved, in the direction this shelf had NOT recorded

`git ls-remote` per candidate, because a slug that resolves is a real repository whatever a list says.

```

```

🔴 **The holder IS in the licence text, dated and plainly stated, and the instrument answered "not
answerable".** 🔵 **Why it survived:** the control for that branch is `moodle/moodle`'s real

`HOLDER-MATCH / Gibbon Foundation` is what the repository supports — asserted under the MIT family,
so it proved nothing about the GPL path where the question actually lives.** An invented payload that

control:** its real Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` fills the appendix with **`Copyright 2025 Data Intelligence

this base could not see it.** 🟡 The verdict is `HOLDER-UNRELATED` and that is the instrument's honest
limit, not a fork signal: `HKUDS` *is* HKU's Data Science group and no token test bridges the acronym.

🟢 **Three fixes, each measured rather than read, and the second was `D7`'s own defect re-committed:**

1. 🔴 The `SENTENCE` guard is a **lexical floor** and the real GPL text walks through it:
   `'on the Program, and are irrevocable provided the stated'`. **Not one of its words is on the
   list.** 🟢 Replaced by a **structural** predicate — three or more consecutive all-lowercase words
   is prose, whatever the words are — explicitly **not** *"starts lowercase"*, which would reject
   `openSUSE Project` and `ownCloud GmbH`.
2. 🔴 **Letting every copyleft text fall through to `holder()` re-opened exactly what `D7` closed**:
   `DeepTutor`'s Apache payload then published `'statement to Your modifications and'` as a holder.
   🟢 So the appendix reader is the **DATED** one, which is structural: a filled notice carries a
   **year** between `Copyright` and the name, and body prose does not.
3. 🔴 Even the structural run-length rule left **one** survivor, `'are not'` — two words, below the
   threshold. 🟢 A **name carries a capital or a digit**; a multi-word candidate with neither is
   prose. Single lowercase words are left alone, so `tldraw` survives.

### 🔴 The most decision-relevant APAC fact is a failure, and it is the best argument this base has

**South Korea built, deployed and then unwound a national AI digital-textbook programme** — status
revoked by the National Assembly **four months into rollout** (Aug 2025); adoption 🔴 **37% → 19%**;
**two data-protection violations** found by the privacy regulator; the **state auditor found the
textbooks were brought into schools without a pilot**; publisher suits **dismissed** (Jul and Aug 2026);
the review process for 2026-year products **halted**.

🔴 **Not one cited cause was model capability** — factual errors, privacy, screen time and teacher
workload are all **implementation and governance failures, inside a delivery partner's scope.** 🟢 **It
makes three claims testable: a mandate is not adoption** (the decline happened *while* the mandate
stood), **a privacy finding outranks an accuracy benchmark**, and **the pilot is not a formality.**
New patterns **`P30`** (brief APAC per jurisdiction — there is no APAC requirement) and **`P31`** (the
pilot-gated rollout, built backwards from this reversal, with synthetic pilot data and the teacher half
shipped first). Trends **`T53`**, **`T54`**.

⚠️ **GRADE: SECONDARY-CONVERGENT, PRIMARY UNREAD — all five.** 🔴 **`mext.go.jp`, `moe.gov.sg`,
`moe.go.kr`, `cbse.gov.in`, `pib.gov.in` and `www.gov.uk` are DNS-unresolvable from this sandbox**
(`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`); only `github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` resolve. **This base does
not publish a licence it has not read, and it marks a regulation it could not read either.**

🔴 **`p276`'s `47/47` is refuted by execution, and so are both of its expected counts** — it predicted
`VERIFIED-ABSENT=48 · QUEUE-UNENUMERATED=70`; the gate, once fixed, reports **53** and **69**. Its
*evidence* half (plain `git` + `curl` at pinned SHAs) stands; its *instrument* half was labelled
`UNVERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION`, has now been tested, and failed. 🟢 **The label is what made this measurable
in one command.**

🔴 **The gate could not say WHAT failed, because `Makefile:31` ran the suite as `>/dev/null`**,
discarding the `# N FAILING:` report the suite exists to print. **Third member of a family this Makefile
documents in its own comments:** `p253`'s gate could not **hear** its controls, `p254`'s could not
**speak** its verdict, 🔴 **`p277`'s could not SEE what failed.**

🟢 **Fixed, and the fix paid for itself in the same run — the suite named its own defect in one line:**

```
# 1 FAILING:
  FAIL a DEAD slug does not own a claim about the real repo of the same basename:
       got [], want ['Gego-K12/gegok12']
```

🟢 **So the defect was READ before it was patched, and then patched (`D6`).** `p275` widened
`attribute()` to match a bare repository name; `p276` narrowed it to be **case-sensitive**, correctly
killing thirteen false refutations caused by `lms` matching *"a proprietary **LMS**"*. 🔴 **That

## Pass 275 — 2026-10-17 — **THE POSITIVE CONTROL `p274` ORDERED PASSED CLEANLY, AND RUNNING IT IS STILL HOW THE REAL DEFECT SURFACED: A PATH LADDER CANNOT PROVE ABSENCE**

⏱️ **Twenty-first pass of `2026-10-17`.** Evidence:
[`tree-enumeration.2026-10-17-p275.tsv`](evidence/tree-enumeration.2026-10-17-p275.tsv) — **13 slugs,

**14 manifests, every one read at payload, zero searches** ·
[`verified-repos.2026-10-17-p275.tsv`](evidence/verified-repos.2026-10-17-p275.tsv) ·
[`p275-websearch.2026-10-17-p275.tsv`](evidence/p275-websearch.2026-10-17-p275.tsv) — **8 legs**.

### 🟢 Headline: the agent this base told studios they could not use has been MIT all along, and it says so twelve times

`p274` ranked one item first, at zero searches: *"re-probe every negative licence verdict with
`ls-remote` as a positive control — the mechanism that produced the `gegok12` false negative is not
specific to that row."*

🟢 **It was run over all 13 negative-verdict slugs, and it returned a clean negative result: the
mechanism is NOT endemic.** `gegok12/gegok12` fails `ls-remote` with `rc=128` exactly as a nonexistent
repository does, and **all twelve other slugs resolve.** 🔴 **Then the same sweep refuted two of this
base's own published verdicts — for a different reason entirely.**

| row | what this base published | what enumerating the tree found |
|---|---|---|
| **`ls1intum/Athena`** | *"no grant across **76 path/ref probes** over three passes; treat as **all-rights-reserved**; ask TUM for the licence in writing"* | 🔴 **12 of 14 manifests declare `license = "MIT"`**, unanimous. Now the **24th permissive row** |
| **`os4ed/openSIS-Classic`** | *"no licence payload served on any path tried"*, carried multiple passes | 🔴 **`docs/License.txt` — verbatim GPL-2.0, HTTP 200, 17 286 B.** Published as false in **five places across three shelves** |

🔴 **Both failures were structurally guaranteed, not unlucky.** Athena's root `pyproject.toml` — the
exact path the ladder probed, four refs over — is a **632-byte Poetry workspace stub containing zero
occurrences of the string `license`**. It is the one manifest in the repository that is silent. openSIS's
grant is at **mixed case *and* `.txt` *and* under `docs/`**; an earlier cell recorded *"no payload in 17
filenames"* and **the 17 did not include it**.

### 🔴 The defect species — and the worst part: THIS BASE ALREADY HELD THE PRINCIPLE, AND THE CODE

🔴 **The method below is not new to this base, and that is the finding.**
[`compose/code/p275-tree-enumeration/`](compose/code/p275-tree-enumeration/) — **pase 93,
`2026-10-04`** — states it outright, and ships a working blobless-clone enumerator (`sweep_tree.sh`):

> **`P275`**: *para sostener una ausencia en un árbol hay que ENUMERARLO.*
> **`P278`**: *un conteo de CERO sobre una ruta que no existe en esa ref mide la RUTA, no el contenido.*

🔴 **`P278` describes this pass's two false negatives exactly** — openSIS's grant is at a path the ladder
never spelled, Athena's at a manifest the ladder never reached — **and the principle, the corollary and
the instrument had all been sitting in `compose/code/` for ~180 passes.** They were applied to
**directory** trees (ILIAS components, `frappe`, `openeducat`) and **never to licence paths**, where the
work went on extending ladders instead: `p267`'s `19 × 4`, `p273`'s `ACTION YU`.

🔵 **`p274` wrote this pass's diagnosis and did not apply it to itself:** *"a correction applied to one
instance is not a correction to the class."* **`P275` was the correction; licences were the instance it
never reached.** **Seventh consecutive pass whose defect species was invisible to the check written one
pass earlier — and the first in which the lesson was already written on this base in GENERAL form, with
code, and was simply never carried across domains.**

🟢 **So the fix was not to invent a method. It was to apply `P275` where it had never been applied:**

```
git ls-remote <slug> HEAD                                    # positive control: does it resolve?
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout <slug>   # blobless, seconds
git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD                               # EVERY path.  No guessing.
```

### 🟢 What a studio can do today that it could not yesterday

**Artemis (MIT) + Iris (MIT) + Pyris (MIT) + Athena (MIT, metadata)** is one permissively-graded
automated-feedback stack from TU Munich — platform, tutor, LLM microservice **and the grading engine**.

### 🔴 And the standing gate was RED at `HEAD`, which no pass-273 artefact mentions

🟢 **`p274` ran `make hooks` — and it failed, on the committed tree, before this pass had changed
anything.** Proven rather than asserted: `git stash` → the identical **6 of 166** controls fail → `git
stash pop`.

```
6/166 FAILED
  - ordering on agents/top.md is AGREE or UNDECIDABLE (reference doc)
  - agents/top.md: if it carries dated sections they are ordered
  - ordering on repos/foundations.md …            (and the same pair)
  - ordering on verticals/solutions.md …          (and the same pair)
```

🔵 **The mechanism, and it is a slow-growing defect rather than a mistake.** `p261`'s invariant is that a
shelf carrying two or more pass-numbered `##` headings must carry them **non-increasing in file order** —
the shape a shelf has when each pass **prepends**. 🔴 **These three reference docs were built by passes
that APPENDED**, so their pass numbers ran `273, 269, 268, 270, 272` (`agents/top.md`), `270, 272`
(`repos/foundations.md`) and `270, 271, 272` (`verticals/solutions.md`). **Each append was individually
harmless; the second one in ascending order tripped the invariant, and it has been red since.**

🟢 **Fixed by permuting the pass sections into descending order within their existing positions** —
content untouched, non-pass sections untouched — and `make hooks` now exits **0** with **45 PASS**.
⚠️ **One consequence recorded because it bit this pass's own prose:** the permutation **moves line
numbers**, so a finding must cite a **row and a section**, never a line number. Three of this pass's own
sentences had to be rewritten for exactly that reason.

🔴 **The deeper point is why nobody noticed.** `p261`'s own section records that the gate *"ran for the
first time in ten passes"* and was red then too; `p251` and `p252` both recorded `make` as **not runnable
from their session**. 🔵 **A gate that is only run when someone remembers is a gate whose verdict is
unknown**, and the invariant it enforces is precisely the kind no reader notices. 🟢 **`make hooks` now
also runs `make recount`** (`T43`), so the two cheapest checks on this base share one entry point.

### 🟢 `T39` — this base measures licence bytes, and bytes discriminate nothing

`OpenOLAT` is the row this KB tells a studio to use when procurement excludes copyleft, so its grant
deserved more than a label. Measured **10,982 B** against stock Apache-2.0's **11,357 B** — 🔵 **a *short*

entire `TERMS AND CONDITIONS` is byte-identical to upstream**; the missing span is the **optional
APPENDIX**, replaced by two attribution notes with no legal effect. **Rider-cleared.**

**10,273 B → 11,525 B** — a **1,252 B range straddling stock in both directions** — and **all six are
unmodified**. ⚠️ **No byte count, high or low, carries information about what a grant says.** It detects
that a payload *changed* between passes; it cannot say *what it says*. **Agreement "to the byte" proves
stability, not correctness.**

*"Recorded in `intel/market.md` and `intel/trends.md`."*

```
$ grep -c "Sanoma" intel/market.md intel/trends.md
intel/market.md:0
intel/trends.md:0
```

🔴 **It was in neither.** This is the **fifth cross-shelf defect in five passes** and a **new
species**: the four before it were omissions — silence, which a grep finds. **This one was a
sentence that answered the grep**, and it suppressed its own detection: `p269`'s backlog sweep
**did not list Sanoma, because this base said it was already shelved.**

🟢 **The amendment is one line, now `T29`:** `p268` amended the **novelty** check to grep the
*slug*; **`p270` amends the *propagation* check to grep the DESTINATION file and never to trust a
claim in the source file.** 🔵 **The same defect class turned up in a second file the same day** —
`intel/policy-matrix.tsv` declares *"VERDICT vocabulary (closed)"* with **five** values and the
column actually carries **twelve**. `HIGH_RISK` and `FRAMEWORK_LAUNCHED` were findable **only by
counting**. Header now reconciled: **12 declared, 12 present, zero undeclared.**

### 🔴 And the generalisation, which is the part worth taking to a client

**Five errors, and not one of them pointed toward understatement.** A mock-Senate exercise gained
the word *"Act"*. A two-year-old guidebook became the current position. A real report acquired a
cleaner title than the one it has. A two-publisher range collapsed into a point. One aggregator
citing no source became a three-country finding.

🔵 **The mechanism is compression, not carelessness.** Restatement drops **qualifiers** — status,
date, publisher, sample — and keeps the **claim**; a claim without its qualifiers reads stronger
than its evidence. 🟢 **So a client knowledge base maintained by restatement is systematically
overconfident, and the overconfidence concentrates in exactly the cells a slide quotes. The audit
that catches it is not an audit of the summary — it is re-running the original query.** Budget one
re-verification pass per six carried datums and expect roughly five to move. New trend **`T31`**.

### 🟢 The best commercial sentence on this base, finally shelved

**Sanoma, >20,000 teachers, 14 countries: 63% of European teachers use AI — and only 16% believe
general-purpose AI improves learning outcomes.** A **47-point gap**. 🔵 **The pitch is not "adopt
AI"**; that argument is won and the client has receipts that it did not help. It is *"the
general-purpose assistant your teachers already use does not know your curriculum, your assessment
rules or your exam board."* New trend **`T28`** and new pattern **`P20`** — the Spain/LOMLOE
teacher-workflow engagement, built on `OpenDidactia` (**CC BY-SA 4.0**, verified at payload) read as
a **specification** rather than shipped as content, with the ShareAlike boundary drawn explicitly.

  `p269` said spend them last. **`p270` spent them not at all** and used the budget on the backlog.

  ZERO rows.** Both already clear the five-row minimum many times over. **Fewer real rows beat
  padding.**
- 🔴 **`Gap 367` was tested in a third language (Spanish) and the closure held a third time.** Nine
  repositories, eight university student course portfolios, the ninth already held. **There is still
  no permissively licensed primary-band AI-literacy curriculum in any of four languages.**
- ⚠️ **No primary source was attempted**, per `p268`'s standing instruction. **Every regional and
  market figure in this pass is secondary-source grade and says so in its own cell.**

🟡 **Named for `p271`, costed:** the EMEA result means **NA's `$3.68B` and MEA's `$0.56B` are the
obvious next re-verification targets** — each rests on **one** publisher and neither has ever been

### 🔴 A licence can be inherited from a project template — a third axis of licence risk

`ai-edu-for-kids` declares CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and then says, verbatim:
*"注：默认使用CC 4.0协议，也可根据自身项目情况选用其他协议"* — **"CC 4.0 is used by default; you may
choose another licence depending on your project."**

🔴 **The most restrictive attribute of the most relevant artefact in this category is boilerplate
carried over from an organisation's project template — not a decision anyone made about this
course.** `T20` grades a grant by its *shape*; this is **provenance**: who chose it, and whether
anyone chose it at all. 🔵 Two consequences pointing opposite ways, both in new trend **`T27`**:
**never assume it away** (a default is legally identical to a deliberate NC-SA), **and** it is the
licence **most likely to move if asked** — unlike `PageLM`'s or `AStheTECH`'s bespoke grants, which
were chosen *for* a reason.

🔴 **The row was invisible to any organisation-level check.** `datawhalechina` already appears on
**two shelves** here; the **slug** `ai-edu-for-kids` returned **zero hits in every file of this
base.** That is `p268`'s `code-dot-org` lesson — *grep the slug, not the prose claim* — firing one
pass later, in a second language, against a different organisation. **Measured twice now, not argued
once.**

grants** (`PrairieLearn` — AGPL-3.0 CE *plus* a separate-terms Enterprise directory *plus* MIT
portions *plus* AGPL client-side JS), **exception lists with a commercial member**
(`RunestoneInteractive/rs` — MIT over the **commercial** Handsontable component), **open-core**
(the Moodle MCP server), and **spelling/location** (`LICENCE`, or a grant living only in
`package.json`). 🔵 **Two cheap rules:** a sidebar License link with **no label** is a *signal*, not
a missing datum; and read the payload's **first paragraph**, since pass 266's title-region rule
answers *which licence* but never *over which files*. New trend **T20**.

### 🔴 The headline: a denial that does not bill is not a budget

🟢 **`p254` was the pass that broke a sixteen-pass inheritance** — it tried the other transport and found the `403` *wall* was a closed door. 🔴 **And in the same pass it published a replacement rule its own numbers could have refuted:** *"treat a `403` from this channel as budget exhausted until `rate_limit` says otherwise."*

🟢 **`p255` read the meter on both sides of the refusal.**

| | |
|---|---|
| `rate_limit` via `WebFetch`, before | `core` `limit 60`, **`remaining 51`**, `used 9` |
| four `/repos/{slug}` calls, same minute | 🔴 **`403` × 4** |

🔵 **And the probe nobody had run is the static one:** `api.github.com/licenses/mit` is `403` through the proxy, and it contains no repository at all. 🟢 **So the two transports are two IDENTITIES, held by two different gates:**

| transport | identity | the gate | what it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curl` through the session proxy | 🟢 **authenticated, `15 000`/h** | a **repository-scope allow-list** | `/repos/gmilano/*` `200`; every other owner, all `/search/*`, `/users/*`, `/orgs/*` and `/licenses/*` → `403` |

🟢 **`ACTION RP`, p221's registered highest-priority action for this pass, swept the first `40` of `247` bare-GNU rows against up to `9` prescribed channels on two branches. Limb `1` wanted `20`+ to resolve to an explicit bound.**

🔴 **And then the premise inverts.** `-only` / `-or-later` is **SPDX's** notation. Four other grammars are in use on these shelves, and in two of them the bound is carried by **omission**:

| grammar | `or-later` | `only` |
|---|---|---|
| **SPDX** *(`composer.json`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`)* | `GPL-3.0-or-later` | `GPL-3.0-only` · 🔵 **bare = nothing said** |
| **CRAN** *(`DESCRIPTION`)* | `GPL (>= 3)` | 🔴 **`GPL-3` — bare IS the only-form** |
| **Odoo** *(`*/__manifest__.py`)* | `'LGPL-3 or any later version'` | 🔴 **`'LGPL-3'` — bare IS the only-form** |
| **PyPI trove** | `… v3 or later (AGPLv3+)` | `… v3 (AGPLv3)` |
| **prose** *(a GNU header)* | *"any later version"* | *"(non-upgradable)"* |

🔴 **p221's `parse_range()` reads a bare `GPL-3` as `unspecified` in all five. For SPDX and prose that is right; for CRAN and Odoo it is wrong.** 🟢 **So `2 208` is the correct count of bare **tokens** and is not the count of unspecified **grants** → `ACTION RU`, the registered highest priority for p223, re-runs the census under the grammar, offline.**

### 🆕 🟢 The headline: `ACTION QV` asked a risk question and the cheap half of it was a reading question

🔴 **`ACTION QV`, the registered highest-priority action for this pass, asked whether the `47` licence-unknown rows sit on a reciprocal upstream — *"a dead end even if the author answers."* It fires: `6` of `47` name one on a token grep, `4` of `47` are installed INTO one. 🔴 **Then the conclusion inverts. `3` of those `4` were never ungranted.** 🟢 **The ecosystem that makes a repo reciprocal is the same ecosystem that prescribes WHERE its licence goes — WordPress in `readme.txt` and the plugin header, Moodle in `version.php` and the file docblocks, Magento in `composer.json`. 🔴 **This reverses an order of work that has been stuck for `15` passes.** 🔴 **`ACTION PH` — *"ask the maintainer to commit a `LICENSE` body"* — would have asked `3` of these `4` authors for a file they had already shipped, under a different name, in the place their ecosystem puts it.** 🟢 **Identify the upstream → read its convention → only then consider asking a human. ### 🔴 This pass's own defect, caught by its own cross-check — and p199 is vindicated

p200's first licence read said **`AGPL-3.0`** for Moodle, Chamilo, ILIAS and H5P. **p199 had
published `GPL-3.0`.** 🟢 **p199 is right.**

> **The GPL-3.0 text contains the phrase *"GNU Affero General Public License"* in its own § 13.**
> Any classifier that decides the family by searching for that phrase calls **every** GPL-3.0
> repository AGPL.

🔴 **And the defect is intermittent, which is why it survives review:** the same detector read
`frappe/erpnext` correctly from an identical licence, because the two copies **wrap § 13
differently** — a line-oriented grep over wrapped legal text is not a classifier. 🟢 **The clean
discriminator, measured on `8` blobs with no overlap: count of `affero` = `3` (incidental, § 13)
for GPL-3.0 versus `15` for AGPL-3.0**, title line agreeing. `Gap 450`, `ACTION OI`.

🔵 **Why it mattered enough to re-check rather than publish:** GPL vs AGPL is the difference
between *"a client may host this"* and *"hosting it may compel disclosure."* 🟢 **The shape is
p199's own `openedx/XBlock` episode with the roles reversed — a later pass "correcting" an
earlier one that was right — and p199 wrote the rule for exactly this case.**

### 🆕 🔴 The fourth number that measured its reader: this pass's own byte counts

🔴 **Python text mode applies UNIVERSAL NEWLINES.** Reading a licence as text and reporting
`len(text.encode())` loses **one byte per CRLF line**, so the figure is the LF-normalised
length, not the file's size:

```
  BranchingScenario font LICENSE.txt   wc -c = 11 560   text-mode = 11 358   CRLF = 202
```

🟢 **`11 560 − 11 358 = 202`, exactly the CRLF count.** 🟢 **Blast radius, measured rather than
assumed: ONE row.** Every other text read this pass — all `30` root-licence rows, all `3` root
payloads, the other `13` `Lumi` texts — is LF, `delta 0`, so 🟢 **every byte figure in the
tables below stands**, and the `3` root payloads are independently confirmed byte-for-byte by
p197.

🔴 **But the band table was computed from these counts**, so a CRLF row would have shifted a
ratio silently. 🟢 **The fix is in `p198-title-line-family/`: read in BINARY, report `len(raw)`,
and report the CRLF count alongside it** so a reflowed text is visible as reflowed rather than
showing up as a band failure. 🔵 [`evidence/crlf-byte-undercount.2026-10-14-p198.tsv`](evidence/crlf-byte-undercount.2026-10-14-p198.tsv).

🔵 **The lesson, and it is the same one three times over now:** `GPL-2.0`'s preamble made a
*window* report the wrong family; a filename list made a *first match* report the wrong file;
text mode made a *byte count* report the wrong size. 🟢 **Every one is a reader's property
published as the world's.**

| | the record | the actor |
|---|---|---|
| [`openfun/ralph`](https://github.com/openfun/ralph) 🟢 `MIT` *(🆕 `LICENSE.md` `1 094` B — `LICENSE` itself `404`s)* | 🟢 `409 CONFLICT` on **both** write paths, raised before the backend write, documented in a source comment | 🔴 `statements_are_equivalent` compares `{actor, verb, object, id, result, context, attachments}` + `timestamp`/`version` **only when in both** — and excludes **`authority`** and `stored` by name |
| [`openedx-mcp`](https://pypi.org/project/openedx-mcp/) 🔴 `AGPL-3.0` | 🟢 `add` blocked, `change` blocked, every field readonly, audit before write | 🔴 `delete` open *(default permission + default bulk action)*, and `SET_NULL` cascades erase attribution |

🟢 **So p189's trend is CORRECTED, not confirmed — and the corrected version is the sellable
one.** *"Nobody protects the record"* is refutable by anyone who has read either codebase.
🟢 ***"The record is protected and the actor is not"*** is true in both, demonstrable from
source, and it is exactly what a regulator, a DPO or an exam board asks — because a trail
that cannot say **who** is not a trail. 🟢 **Pattern `36` is the response**, and steps `1`–`4`
are a READ, so they quote at fixed price.

🔵 **On `ralph` the consequence is not the one the falsifier predicted.** Because equivalence
means **no write at all**, a re-`PUT` differing only in `authority` answers **`204` and is
silently DISCARDED** — a client cannot tell *"stored"* from *"dropped because another
authority already claimed that id"*. 🟢 Integrity intact; attribution swallowed. The fix is
one guard at ingest, not weeks of work.

### 🔴 The finding to take into a client conversation

🔴 **The human-oversight audit record is the artefact nobody is protecting.**
`dotty-tutor`'s `teacher_review_events` is well designed where it counts — `action` is
`CHECK`-constrained to `('reviewed','overturned','mastery_override')` — but
🔴 **`corrected_assessment`, the teacher's overturning of an AI grade, is `ondelete="CASCADE"` from
TWO parents** *(`learning_classes` and `assignments`)*, while `knowledge_point_id` has no
`ondelete` at all. 🔵 **Course-shaped schemas make the class the aggregate root and cascade
everything under it: right for pedagogy, wrong for audit.** 🟢 Three regimes now require that
record — NA *(Oklahoma, Maryland)*, EU *(high-risk assessment)* and 🔴 **Vietnam, the second
jurisdiction to put educational assessment in a statutory high-risk tier.** 🟢 Pattern `32` is the
fix, and step `2` — moving the log out of the course aggregate — is the whole value.

### 🔴 New licence traps, and a correction this KB owes itself

- 🔴 **`P1054` — MIT's body with a clause bolted on.** [`willwearing/graspful`](https://github.com/willwearing/graspful)'s
  *"O'Saasy License Agreement"* is MIT verbatim plus an anti-SaaS non-compete. 🔴 **Not open
  source**, and 🔴 **every body-matching classifier on this shelf returns `MIT` for it.** 🟢 New
  instrument, `14` tests passing, validated against live bytes:
  [`compose/code/p1054-mit-plus-clause`](compose/code/p1054-mit-plus-clause/README.md).
  🔵 Discriminator is two-signal — restriction vocabulary decides, size catches the rest *(canonical
  MIT measured at `1 062`–`1 093` B over `15` genuine rows; `graspful` is `1 439`)*.
- 🔴 **`P971`, instances three and four**: `numbas-lti-provider` *(`Apache-2.0` in `560` B)* and
  `moodle-block_atrisk` *(`GPL-3` in `703` B)*. 🔵 Say **"by reference"**, not "Apache-2.0" — §`3`,
  the patent grant, is the only strong reason to prefer it and it travels as a URL.
- 🔴 **And the instrument failure: this pass's first sweep returned `NO-GRANT-FOUND` for `36` of
  `36` repositories.** `git ls-remote --symref` emits **two** lines ending `<TAB>HEAD`, the first
  being `ref: refs/heads/main`; the SHA field read `ref:` and every `raw` URL `404`'d. 🟢 Fixed and
  validated against a positive control *(`fsrs4anki-helper` → `MIT`, `1 079` B, `License` — p186's
  own published value, reproduced)*. 🔵 **Rule: a probe returning the SAME verdict for every row has
  measured nothing. Run a known-positive through any sweep before believing it.**

### 🔴 `P146-D` — the finding this pass exists for

`P145-A` is the strongest finding this shelf has produced: an exclusion list four lines
above the one being audited had removed seven of eight rows from a tier, and what was left
behind looked like a measurement. p145 fixed it in its successor and named the class `T42`.

🔴 **What p145 did not ask is whether anything else on the shelf could do the same, or
whether anything would notice.** Both answers are bad.

| | count |
|---|---|
| instruments that traverse a tree | **35** |
| …that carry an **empty-walk guard** | 🔴 **0** |
| …that exclude `dist`/`build`, have no re-admission, and emit a verdict | 🔴 **5** |
| …that cannot read anything but a git clone | 🔴 **16** |

🔵 **The exclusion list was one instrument's bug; the inability to notice is the shelf's.**
A guard is four lines and needs no judgement, because the question it asks has one right
answer in every artefact kind: *did I read anything at all?* `p146-empty-walk-guard`
answers it, and `walked_or_refuse` is wired to preserve the distinction that `P145-A`'s
seven rows collapsed —

| state | meaning | correct output |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **zero files walked** | the instrument saw no input | **no verdict is available** |
| 🟢 **files walked, none matched** | the instrument saw input and found no surface | `NOT_AN_MCP_SERVER` — a finding |

🔴 **`P145-A`'s rows were the first state, published as the second**, and `P146-B` shows a
second instrument standing ready to do it again on the agent tier.

### 🔴 `P143-C` — the finding this pass exists for

`ACTION DM` was a repair. It named two blind shapes and attached a share-based falsifier: *more
than five points on any tier and `T30`'s figures are withdrawn.* The share moved 17 points, so the
falsifier did its job.

🔴 **But the repair's own first draft was wrong in the same way p141 was**, and the falsifier could
not have told anyone. It reported the same 23 `legacy_reference/` sites, merely relabelled
`LITERAL` instead of `DYNAMIC`. 🔴 **Same population, same count, opposite classification — and an
identical tier share.** A five-point test passes that silently.

🟢 **What caught it was noticing that one subject's verdict flipped between two instruments, and
then opening the repository and counting.** 🔵 **A per-subject disagreement is louder than a tier
aggregate**, and the aggregate was the only thing being watched. `T37` states the rule;
`NOT_SHIPPED` and `test_not_shipped_trees_are_excluded` enforce it; and the probe now emits
`not_shipped_delta` per row so a whole-tree/shipped-tree disagreement is visible per subject.

### 🔴 `P142-F`/`P142-G` — the finding this pass exists for

`ACTION DH` was a scale-up. It ran p141's offset channel over 44 connector rows and asked for the
LATAM count *"explicitly, including when it is zero"*, reasoning that *"an eleventh null on 43
rows is a far stronger statement than a tenth on eight."*

🔴 **It returned 0 of 44 — and 0 North America of 44.** p141's table books an offset only where
that offset is unambiguous across the five regions, and the offsets of Brazil, Argentina, Peru,
Mexico, the United States and Canada are precisely the shared ones. 🔵 **The rule is honest; its
refusals are not randomly distributed.** They land on two whole regions, every time, by
construction.

🔵 **North America is what made it legible.** Nobody reading a shelf that carries
`SleepyPandas/UofT-MCP`, `skhdemo/uoft-quercus-mcp` and `luca-dupont2/mcgill-vsb-mcp` would
accept "no North American row" as a measurement of the world — and it comes out of the same rule
for the same reason. 🔴 **An eleventh LATAM null would have been this KB's most confident
restatement of its own blind spot.**

So the pass answered the question on p140's already-proved channel instead — **a hostname the
connector must reach to work** — and 16 of the 19 refusals resolve:

|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **LATAM** | 🟢 **13** | **Brazil 9** (`sigaa.ufpi.br`, `sigaa.ufrn.br`, `suap.ifrn.edu.br`, `ifma.edu.br` …), **Argentina 3** (`siu.edu.ar`, `guarani.unq.edu.ar`, `servicios.unl.edu.ar`), **Peru 1** (16 × `upc.edu.pe`) |

| UNMAPPED | 3 | 2 with no country-bearing host, 1 `.edu`-only |

which someone committing at `-0300` against `sigaa.ufpi.br` is in Greenland.

### `P139-B` — why the write axis is the finding and the count is not

An undocumented read tool is a missing paragraph. 🔴 **An undocumented `bulk_update_grades` is an
ungoverned capability** — and *"grading or ranking learners"* is named high-risk by **EU AI Act
Annex III** and by **Vietnam's Decision 33/2026/QĐ-TTg**, the only education-AI conformity regime
actually in force (`T16`). 🔵 **A duty cannot be discharged against a capability nobody has
enumerated, and the README is what procurement reads.** That is why this pass adds **`P18`**, a
gate, rather than a caveat on `P17`: pull the payload, count registered tools across all three
registration idioms, diff against the documentation, partition by write verb, then call `tools/list`
on the running server and diff again — because registration is not behaviour.

🔴 **`@imazhar101/mcp-canvas-server` is the row that should stop a delivery conversation**: 227
tools, 96 documented, **61 undocumented writes**, including **`update_sso_settings`** and
**`restore_authentication_provider`** — tools that change how a Canvas tenant authenticates — in the
same package p138 found carrying **no licence signal and no `repository` field**, so there is no
source to audit either.

### `P139-C` — the one that changes delivery, and it moved the cost rather than removing it

p138 wrote of its own `ACTION CE`: *"answered by reading an interface, not by calling it."* `ACTION CL`
called it. 🟢 **The brokered flow does not demand the Canvas redirect when a grant is pre-seeded** —
proven by a sentinel listener standing in for Canvas and recording **zero** connections, with the
grant store encrypted at rest (`scrypt` + AES-GCM, no plaintext). 🔴 **But the integration shape is
not what p138 implied**: because `main()` runs on import, an embedder cannot pass `oauthStore` in
process. The working route is **seed the encrypted store, run `serve` as a managed process**. `P13`
is rewritten a fifth time: 🟢 **protocol work drops to hours, plumbing rises to ~a week**, and the
"no fork" claim is **narrowed, not refuted** — no fork to *use* it, a one-line `main` guard to
*embed* it.
